rv.q: Out of a night of wonderful moments, the one that haunts me is Millonzi — one of Off Broadway’s sharpest weapons — as Emilia, her face in shadow, talking bitterly about the wrongs men do women.
You don’t need bells and whistles to make great theater.
Bedlam gets props for once again letting us see a classic work in new ways.
Tucker’s Othello is a bell-ringing winner and, to mix metaphors, a lengthy feather in Bedlam’s cap.
But on the other hand, this Othello is not Bedlam at its best.
With so few actors playing so many roles, it's harder to identify with any one of them for very long, to put ourselves in their shoes and imagine how we too might become that monster.

cn.t: Bedlam's bare-bones four-actor "Othello" earns mostly positive reviews for its skilled ensemble and inventive staging, though some critics question the stripped-down approach and miss the company's usual playful energy.
